stories.body: Yemen's internationally recognised government said Houthi ballistic missiles and drones targeted Aden International Airport, with one missile landing near the runway shortly before a flight from Cairo was due to arrive. The flight was diverted to Jeddah, the terminal was evacuated and aircraft were moved from the tarmac. The Houthis said they had targeted Saudi military supplies near the airport, while the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a separate missile north of Riyadh. The attacks come as Saudi-backed government forces press a counteroffensive around Mocha and the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait, with fighting concentrated in southwestern Taiz province.
stories.headline: Houthi strikes hit Aden airport as fighting intensifies in Yemen

stories.body: Russian drones and missiles struck cities across Ukraine overnight, killing civilians including children and damaging homes, industrial sites and infrastructure, Ukrainian authorities said. Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 130 drones, 48 cruise missiles and an unspecified number of ballistic missiles, while President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described it as one of the largest attacks of the war and said energy infrastructure was a key target. Kyiv, Poltava, Dnipropetrovsk and Kharkiv were among the areas hit; officials reported a deadly strike on an apartment building in Pryluki as well as deaths in Kyiv and central Ukraine. Russia said it had targeted military-industrial, port and ship-repair facilities.
stories.headline: Russian barrage across Ukraine kills civilians and targets energy infrastructure

stories.body: Israel is holding memorial events three years after the Hamas-led October 7, 2023 attacks, the deadliest day in the country's history. Bereaved families and former hostages are commemorating those killed, while some relatives are using the anniversary to demand an independent inquiry and greater accountability from Benjamin Netanyahu's government. The commemorations are taking place under heightened security and as the legacy of the attacks remains central to an approaching election campaign.
stories.headline: Israel marks three years since the October 7 Hamas attacks amid an election campaign

stories.body: France's interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, has temporarily suspended police use of stun grenades at high-school demonstrations after a 15-year-old lost a hand during a protest in Lens. Authorities are investigating the circumstances of the injury, while the minister said the weapons would not be used in the student movement until the facts were established. The decision follows two weeks of protests over teacher shortages, overcrowded and deteriorating schools, and long school days; officials say hundreds of students, school staff and police officers have been injured, and 18 internal investigations into alleged police brutality have been opened.
stories.headline: France suspends police use of stun grenades at student protests after teenager loses hand

stories.body: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry has been awarded to French scientist Henri B. Kagan and Japan's Kenso Soai for work explaining how chemical reactions can favour one mirror-image form of a molecule over the other. This molecular asymmetry, known as chirality, is fundamental to life: amino acids and other biological molecules can exist in left- and right-handed forms, but living organisms use only one. Their research made it possible to design reactions that produce far more of the desired form, an advance with particular importance for medicines because mirror-image molecules can have very different biological effects.
stories.headline: Chemistry Nobel honors research into the molecular asymmetry essential to life

stories.body: Police officers working with Immigration and Customs Enforcement to arrest unauthorized immigrants received a shortened training course that reduced instruction on US immigration law, according to emails reviewed by The Washington Post. The disclosures raise questions about the preparation of local officers deputized to carry out immigration-enforcement functions.
stories.headline: Emails show ICE shortened immigration-law training for deputized local officers

stories.body: The US Supreme Court heard more than two hours of arguments over whether Boulder, Colorado, may proceed with a lawsuit seeking to hold ExxonMobil and Suncor Energy liable for climate-change-related harms. The questioning left it unclear whether a majority of justices would allow the city's novel case to move forward.
stories.headline: Supreme Court weighs whether Boulder can pursue climate-liability case against major oil companies

stories.body: Cornell University leaders may face a Faculty Senate no-confidence vote as the institution confronts criticism over its handling of sexual-assault allegations. An Obama-era Justice Department official will lead an outside review. Reporting on campus data found that incidents at Cornell are more likely to be reported to law enforcement than statewide figures suggest, but less likely to result in serious discipline, amid a broader rise in reported sexual violence at colleges.
stories.headline: Cornell faces mounting scrutiny over its response to sexual-assault allegations

stories.body: Spain's Constitutional Court has formally notified the Supreme Court of its ruling backing the application of the amnesty law to the misuse-of-public-funds offense tied to the Catalan independence process. The Supreme Court must now examine the ruling and decide how to apply it to former Catalan president Carles Puigdemont, who faces charges but has not been tried, and to other independence leaders including Oriol Junqueras, Dolors Bassa, Raül Romeva, Jordi Turull, Toni Comín and Lluís Puig. The Constitutional Court found that the Supreme Court's earlier refusal to amnesty Bassa violated her right to effective judicial protection.
stories.headline: Spain's Constitutional Court clears the way to apply amnesty to Puigdemont and other Catalan independence leaders

stories.body: Spain's major unions, CCOO and UGT, are planning a 24-hour nationwide general strike on November 11 over wages and housing, the first such strike backed by the country's largest labor organizations in 14 years. Housing groups helped drive the call after protests over evictions and housing policy. The date falls two days before the start of campaigning for the November 29 general election, a timing chosen to avoid possible intervention by the electoral authorities, though business groups question whether a strike centered on housing demands meets the legal requirement for a labor dispute.
stories.headline: Spanish unions set nationwide general strike over pay and housing for November 11

stories.body: Spain's government has approved new housing decrees to replace measures rejected by Congress last week, retaining restrictions on speculative purchases of homes acquired below 70% of their appraised value. The revised rules extend the restriction through 2030, broaden it to companies classed as large landlords and related entities with more than 10 properties, and apply it to auctions. They also revise compensation rules when evictions are suspended without alternative housing, making regional governments responsible for prompt payment in relevant cases. The measures return housing policy to the center of debate ahead of the November election.
stories.headline: Spanish government reintroduces housing measures after Congress rejected its previous package

stories.body: Madrid prosecutors have asked the Provincial Court to acquit Begoña Gómez, the wife of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, and her adviser Cristina Álvarez of alleged influence peddling and misuse of public funds. In provisional findings, prosecutors said the allegations related to Gómez's role in a Complutense University chair and associated software project did not constitute criminal offenses, finding no evidence that either woman obtained financial benefit or that the university suffered a financial loss. A popular prosecution led by Hazte Oír is seeking prison terms, while the defense also seeks acquittal.
stories.headline: Prosecutors seek acquittal for Begoña Gómez in Complutense University case

stories.body: Much of Catalonia's Rodalies commuter rail network was halted or severely disrupted after train drivers declined to begin services without updated safety reports following recent storms and an overnight tree strike on a regional train near Vilanova i la Geltrú. Renfe characterized the stoppage as a labor conflict and said services had operated safely, while the main drivers' union said required protocols had not been met. After receiving reports on the condition of the infrastructure, drivers began returning to some routes, but service recovered only gradually, with delays, incomplete coverage, limited replacement buses and widespread confusion among passengers.
stories.headline: Rodalies rail disruption strands Catalan commuters after drivers cite safety concerns

stories.body: Barcelona Mayor Jaume Collboni has declared an emergency over October's torrential rains, which brought nearly 200 liters of water per square meter over the weekend, disrupted transport and caused around 50 landslides, particularly in hillside neighborhoods. The declaration allows the city to contract essential repair and prevention work through emergency procedures. Heavy rain on Tuesday also left 810 Endesa customers without electricity, largely because water entered substations and underground electrical infrastructure; the utility said it was draining affected facilities and repairing faults, while the city has opened an inquiry into earlier outages and is considering sanctions.
stories.headline: Barcelona declares an emergency after torrential rain damage as power outages continue

stories.body: Emergency crews and volunteers continued searching for a 12-year-old boy who disappeared in Granollers on Sunday during the first episode of severe rain. The boy, who has autism, was reportedly frightened by thunder and was last seen in an area southeast of the city spanning urban, agricultural and wooded land. About 470 people joined the operation, involving firefighters, Mossos d'Esquadra, local police, rural agents, dogs, drones and aerial resources, though volunteers were stood down in the evening because of renewed heavy rain.
stories.headline: Search continues for 12-year-old missing in Granollers after severe flooding

stories.body: Hundreds of people gathered outside the Bloc Llenguadoc in Barcelona's Sant Andreu district to try to stop the eviction of dozens of residents, including families with children and other vulnerable people. Housing groups say the building has been occupied since 2017 and residents want to regularize their status through affordable rents; municipal figures indicate that several families with children are receiving social-services support. City and Catalan housing officials sought to mediate with the owner, with Barcelona's housing commissioner calling the eviction inappropriate and unnecessary and saying new housing decrees could provide grounds to halt it.
stories.headline: Hundreds gather in Sant Andreu to prevent eviction of families from Bloc Llenguadoc
